Erdos25.erdos_25: Strictly increasing positive moduli; residue exclusions begin at the modulus. The target asks for logarithmic density for arbitrary such sequences.
The 2026 Ulam/Chojecki manuscript handles summable reciprocal moduli and coprime cases and explicitly leaves the general step open.
Erdos30.erdos_30: The Sidon extremal function differs from sqrt(N) by O_epsilon(N^epsilon) for every positive epsilon. This is stronger than an asymptotic with leading constant one.
PR 3935 records partial bounds and Singer assumptions, leaving this main target open; the newer N^(1/4) error bounds do not suffice.
Erdos52.erdos_52: The sum-product question quantifies over finite sets of integers, not arbitrary real sets.
The 2026 counterexample concerns real sets and does not settle the integer conjecture.
Erdos61.erdos_61: The full Erdos-Hajnal statement quantifies over every fixed forbidden induced graph with an exponent allowed to depend on that graph.
Known results for five-vertex graphs and newer individual forbidden graphs do not establish the universal assertion.
Erdos91.erdos_91: For every sufficiently large cardinality, there must be two non-similar planar configurations attaining the minimum number of distinct distances. The minimum is a natural-number infimum; the real casts in the set builder do not turn it into a real infimum.
Results on a density-one set of cardinalities do not establish the eventual assertion for all cardinalities.
Erdos98.erdos_98: No three collinear and no four concyclic; the minimum distinct-distance count divided by cardinality tends to infinity. The general-position conditions and superlinear conclusion were checked separately.
The recent linear lower bound is weaker. A forum proof attempt was acknowledged to rely on unsupported axioms.
Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero: The selected extension excludes exponent zero, uses coprime bases at least three, and retains the reciprocal-sum condition. This differs from the unit-allowing version.
The existing Aristotle result and PR 4354 concern exponent zero and do not solve the selected extension.
Erdos138.erdos_138: The kth root of the van der Waerden number tends to infinity; a fixed exponential lower bound does not imply it.
The 2026 lower bound of order k times 2^(k-1) and solutions of a difference variant leave this target open.
Erdos168.erdos_168.parts.ii: Irrationality of the limiting extremal ratio, encoded using limsup. Existence of the limit and irrationality are separate questions.
The known formula and numerical value of the limit do not establish irrationality.
Erdos234.erdos_234: Natural densities of normalized consecutive-prime-gap events for every nonnegative real threshold, forming a continuous distribution function.
The exponential distribution predicted conditionally by prime-tuple conjectures is not an unconditional solution.
Erdos287.erdos_287: Distinct increasing denominators greater than one, reciprocal sum exactly one, and a consecutive gap at least three. Strictness and denominator endpoints were checked.
Finite exclusions and the known gap-at-least-two result in PR 5249 do not establish this assertion.
Erdos304.upper_bound: The selected bound is N(b)=O(log log b), not the known lower bound.
PR 5237 formalizes lower-bound metadata; PR 4870 explicitly leaves the main problem unchanged after a related reduction.
Erdos307.erdos_307: Finite sets of primes satisfying the exact reciprocal-product equation. The main target is distinct from the finite-cardinality exclusions.
PRs 5236/4403 only extend exclusions. PR 4479 corrects a false helper in a sibling result; a forum claim's key step was refuted.
Erdos317.erdos_317.variants.claim2: For all sufficiently large N, every nonzero signed harmonic sum with coefficients in {-1,0,1} has absolute value strictly greater than 1/lcm(1,...,N). The strict inequality is essential: the non-strict bound is elementary.
Finite searches and heuristics do not prove the eventual strict bound; the separate c/2^N claim is not substituted.
Erdos400.erdos_400.parts.i: For each fixed k, the summatory function has an asymptotic c_k*x*log(x) with positive c_k. A lower bound is insufficient.
The 2026 work supplies bounds rather than this full asymptotic. The stronger part ii is not also added as another target.
Erdos410.erdos_410: Iterating sigma_1 from n>1, the kth root tends to infinity. The exclusion of n=1 prevents the fixed-point counterexample; k=0 is irrelevant to the eventual limit.
No exact resolution found in the problem page, discussion, or relevant upstream changes.
Erdos413.erdos_413.parts.i: Infinitely many barriers for the number of distinct prime factors omega. The stronger big-Omega version is not counted separately.
The new O(log i) block result is weaker than the exact barrier required here.
Erdos495.erdos_495: Classical Littlewood: for every pair of reals, liminf of n*||n alpha||*||n beta|| is zero. A bounded subsequence prevents an unbounded-real-liminf default-value interpretation.
The new uniform Littlewood counterexamples have different quantifiers and do not settle the classical statement.
Erdos14.erdos_14.parts.i: For each fixed infinite set and every positive epsilon, its nonunique-sum count is bounded below at scale N^(1/2-epsilon). Uniqueness is modulo swapping summands and includes diagonal sums.

Finite computations and conditional structural claims do not solve this. Existing part ii asks for a set with o(sqrt(N)) nonunique sums; it is compatible and independent, not a Sidon-density assertion as the earlier batch report described it.
Erdos647.erdos_647: Existence of n>24 for which max over m<n of m+tau(m) is at most n+2. The strict lower endpoint removes the known small examples.
PR 4407 gives reductions and computations, not a witness or impossibility proof. An older purported solution was refuted for using an unsupported axiom.
Erdos681.erdos_681: For every sufficiently large N there is k such that N+k is composite and its least prime factor exceeds k^2. The prime/composite restriction matters when k=1.
Almost-all heuristics do not cover the required pointwise assertion, including N one below a prime.
Green36.green_36.variants.cks05: The CKS simultaneous double product property uses i != k and arbitrary epsilon, along infinitely many sizes. The product bound forces nonempty families. Checked against CKS Definition 4.1; the other index pattern is excluded.
The cited construction conjecture remains open; no exact construction or impossibility proof found.
Erdos749.erdos_749: Lower density of A+A can be arbitrarily close to one while the ordered representation function stays bounded.
The solved upper-density variant is weaker and does not settle lower density.
Erdos886.erdos_886: For every positive epsilon a uniform bound on divisors in (sqrt(n),sqrt(n)+n^(1/2-epsilon)). Interval endpoints and uniformity in n were checked.
Known epsilon>1/4 cases do not give all positive epsilon; the corrected four-divisor sibling is distinct.
Erdos930.erdos_930: A fixed number of disjoint intervals of positive integers, each sufficiently long with a bound depending on that number, cannot have product a perfect power. The interval hypotheses avoid empty products and zero.
No exact resolution found in the reviewed source and discussion.
Erdos933.erdos_933: The normalized combination of the 2-adic and 3-adic valuations of n(n+1) has infinite limsup. Natural valuations, positivity, and normalization were checked.
A negative forum claim had its proposed bound explicitly refuted; no valid exact solution remained in that exchange.
Erdos944.erdos_944: Vertex-critical k-chromatic graphs for every k>=4, with the stated robust edge-critical-set requirement for arbitrary r.
The k>=5 case is known; k=4 remains. PR 4237 covers a restricted 6-regular r=1 case.
Erdos949.erdos_949: For arbitrary sum-free S in the reals, a continuum-sized A avoiding S whose pairwise sums also avoid S. No measurability or Baire assumption is inserted.
Known results with regularity, Sidon, or smaller-cardinality hypotheses do not establish this general assertion.
Erdos962.erdos_962: The log of the maximum prime-factor-interval length is bounded at exponent 1/2+o(1) in log(n). The finite search cap k<=n is sound: a longer interval starting at m<=n contains a power of two, violating its prime-factor requirement.
The known O(sqrt(n)) length bound is far weaker than the selected subpolynomial target.
Erdos323.erdos_323.parts.ii: For every 1<=m<k, the number of distinct integers represented by m kth powers is at least order x^(m/k). It counts represented values, not tuples.
Independent of the new diagonal lower bound and the active diagonal o(x) upper bound. Existing problem 325 treats three summands and does not imply this full family.
Erdos979.erdos_979: Unbounded limsup of the number of representations as a sum of k prime kth powers, for every k>=2. Ordering changes counts by at most k!, so not unboundedness.
The 2026 cubic result solves k=3 only; the quartic result gives a finite lower bound and explicitly does not generalize to all k.
Erdos1056.erdos_1056: Arbitrarily many consecutive nonempty positive intervals whose products are one modulo a prime. Strictly increasing endpoints force nonempty intervals, and products one forbid crossing multiples of the prime.
Finite k searches and restricted factorial-collision results do not establish arbitrary k. A directly related implication is not separately counted.
Erdos1062.erdos_1062.parts.ii: Irrationality of the density of the specified union of divisor conditions. Limit existence is a distinct issue.
The recent existence/formula discussion explicitly leaves irrationality open.
Erdos1082.erdos_1082.parts.i: A set with no three collinear points determines at least floor(n/2) distinct distances globally. The stronger pinned-distance assertion is not selected.
Harborth's counterexample and its 2026 rediscovery settle the pinned-distance sibling, not this global-count target; small-n verification is partial.
Erdos1113.erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_f: Every Sierpinski number is a perfect power or admits a finite covering set of primes. This is the FFK question, not existence or infinitude of Sierpinski numbers.
PR 4407 and the known classical constructions concern the solved infinitude sibling.
Erdos1175.erdos_1175: For every uncountable cardinal kappa there exists a cardinal mu such that every mu-chromatic graph has a triangle-free subgraph of chromatic number exactly kappa. Subgraph is not induced; mu is existential.
Shelah's consistency obstruction at mu=kappa=aleph_1 does not refute the existential-mu statement. Related odd-cycle and triangle-free coloring results do not resolve it.
Erdos291.erdos_291.variants.shiu_heurist: Natural density zero of indices at which the harmonic numerator is coprime to the relevant lcm.

The forum misstates a complementary set: Wu-Yan obtain conditional upper density one for the indices where the reduced denominator is smaller than the lcm. Even that does not give natural density one. Known infinitude of non-coprime indices is weaker.
Erdos686.erdos_686.variants.twenty_five: The exact quotient of the two separated consecutive products is 25 for some k>=2. This fixes the square value, preserving positivity and division conditions.
Finite exclusions of k do not settle existence. General all-square/all-integer versions are not added as duplicate implication targets.
Erdos890.erdos_890.parts.b: The limsup of the sum of ordinary distinct-prime-factor counts in a fixed consecutive block, normalized by loglog(n)/log(n), equals one for every fixed positive block length.
New work on the liminf in part a does not settle part b. The altered restricted omega_k helper in part a is not used here.
Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.factorial_ad: Finiteness of indices for which n!+1 is powerful. The finite small-index conventions do not affect finiteness.
The ABC-conditional argument does not establish an unconditional solution. This is independent of the factorial-minus-one and active exponential variants.
Erdos936.erdos_936.variants.factorial_su: Finiteness of indices for which n!-1 is powerful. Natural subtraction only affects small indices and not the finiteness question.
Only conditional ABC consequences were found; no implication between this sign and the factorial-plus-one sign establishes either target.
Erdos770.erdos_770.parts.i: For each prime p, the level set h(n)=p has natural density. The infimum ranges over m>2 in extended naturals; conversion of infinity to zero cannot enter a prime level set.
Conditional infinitude of the p=3 level under a Mersenne-prime hypothesis does not establish density for every prime.
Green39.green_39: Uniform fixed-cardinality random subsets of Z/pZ, with floor(sqrt(p)) elements; the covering probability tends to one along primes. The finite probability denominator is nonzero.
Existing translate-covering bounds leave this threshold open.
Green44.green_44: Exactly 1000 increasing primes, floor(p/2) removed classes, and p_max^10<N^9. The integer inequality faithfully avoids fractional powers.
The usual square-root sieve range does not establish this bound.
Green47.green_47: The eventual residue-class bound leads either to sparse growth or whole-set containment in one rational quadratic image of integers.
Croot-Yip's 2026 result gives a large intersection with a quadratic, not whole-set containment.
Green66.green_66: An eventual real-X assertion with the specific constant 1/10. Natural squares suffice because signs do not alter squares.
A known bound with an unspecified constant does not settle this fixed constant.
Erdos323.erdos_323.parts.i: For every k>=1 and epsilon>0, the diagonal represented-value count is bounded below by x^(1-epsilon). Distinct values, not representations, are counted.
Known k=2 asymptotics leave the full family open. This lower bound is compatible with the existing k>2 diagonal o(x) upper bound.
Erdos1101.erdos_1101.parts.i: Existence of a good sequence with polynomial growth. The pinned statement has positive polarity; current upstream negates it to match the conjectured negative answer. Both generated modes preserve the pinned question. Zero/one initial terms cannot trivialize the strict gap condition.
The publicly claimed subexponential construction concerns part ii, which is excluded; it does not supply polynomial growth.
Erdos950.erdos_950.parts.iii: The function is o(log log n). This is compatible with the active assertions of liminf one and infinite limsup.
The conditional O(log log log n) estimate does not establish the unconditional target; discussion of a second-moment step is not a completed proof.
Erdos700.erdos_700.parts.ii: Infinitely many composite n have min_{2<=k<=floor(n/2)} gcd(n,C(n,k)) strictly greater than sqrt(n). The natural infimum is over a nonempty finite set for composite n>=4, and f(n)^2>n is equivalent to the strict real-root inequality. The known prime-square family attains equality and does not solve it.

The public constructions rely on unproved infinitude of special primes or prime pairs. The discussion supplies no unconditional infinite family. PR 5212 corrects only the characterization answer in part i; part ii and its minimum are unchanged. No exact prior solution or active/retired equivalent target found.
